# Aperture — Design System Guidelines

**Source of truth for UI.** Coding agents (Cursor / Build Now) and humans must follow this file over generic aesthetics, invented palettes, or ad-hoc component styles.

| Item | Value |
|------|--------|
| System name | **Aperture** |
| Stack | React + Tailwind CSS + **shadcn/ui** patterns |
| Icons | **Phosphor Icons** (`@phosphor-icons/web`) |
| Themes | Light + Dark (`class` strategy) |
| Direction | LTR + RTL (`dir` on `<html>`) |
| Contrast | WCAG 2.1 AA |

---

## 1. Non‑negotiable rules

1. **Do not invent a new visual language.** Use Aperture tokens, zinc neutrals, and orange brand accents below.
2. **One primary action per view/region.** Prefer `primary` once; supporting actions use `secondary` / `ghost`.
3. **Never encode meaning by color alone.** Pair status with icon + text.
4. **Focus rings are mandatory.** Orange 2px ring + 2px offset — never remove without a visible replacement.
5. **Sentence case for actions;** Title Case for page/nav headers (see §8).
6. **Motion stays in the 150–200ms window** on named easing curves. Honor `prefers-reduced-motion`.
7. **Below 640px**, side **Sheet** becomes bottom **Drawer**.
8. Use **logical CSS** (`ms`/`me`, `border-s`, `start`/`end`) — no hard-coded left/right that breaks RTL.
9. Prefer existing **shadcn/ui** components over custom one-offs.
10. When this file conflicts with a generic “make it pretty” instinct, **this file wins**.

---

## 2. Brand & aesthetic

- **Look:** Clean product UI — zinc surfaces, subtle borders, restrained elevation, orange accent.
- **Not:** Purple gradients, glassmorphism noise, neon glow, heavy multi-layer shadows, random decorative cards.
- **Canvas:** Light `#fafafa` / Dark `#09090b`
- **Surfaces:** Light `#ffffff` / Dark `#18181b` (cards, panels)
- **Brand / primary fill:** `#f97316` (orange-500/600 family); hover darkens in light, lightens in dark
- **Destructive:** Rose (`#e11d48` light / `#fb7185` dark)
- **Fonts:** System UI sans (`ui-sans-serif`, system-ui, Segoe UI, Roboto, Helvetica, Arial); mono for code chips

### Shared shell primitives (Tailwind)

```
CARD = rounded-xl border border-zinc-200 dark:border-zinc-800 bg-white dark:bg-zinc-900
RING = focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-orange-500
       focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-white dark:focus-visible:ring-offset-zinc-950
```

---

## 3. Color tokens

### Semantic roles

| Token | Role | Light | Dark | Use |
|-------|------|-------|------|-----|
| `bg/canvas` | Page canvas | `#fafafa` | `#09090b` | Lowest layer; don’t put long-form text directly on canvas without a surface |
| `bg/surface` | Card / panel | `#ffffff` | `#18181b` | Default elevated container; pair with `border/subtle` |
| `bg/muted` | Inset fill | `#f4f4f5` | `#27272a` | Wells, code blocks, secondary rows |
| `fg/default` | Primary action fill | `#f97316` | `#f97316` | Primary buttons; **white** label/icons for AA |
| `fg/hover` | Primary hover | `#ea580c` | `#fb923c` | Darken in light; lighten in dark |
| `fg/neutral` | Secondary fill | `#e4e4e7` | `#3f3f46` | Secondary / ghost resting fill |
| `text/primary` | Body & headings | `#18181b` | `#fafafa` | ≥ 4.5:1 on surface |
| `text/secondary` | Supporting copy | `#52525b` | `#a1a1aa` | Metadata, helpers (≥ 4.5:1) |
| `text/disabled` | Disabled label | `#a1a1aa` | `#52525b` | Always pair with non-color disabled cues |
| `icon/interactive` | Actionable icon | `#ea580c` | `#fb923c` | ≥ 3:1 graphical contrast |
| `icon/neutral` | Informational icon | `#52525b` | `#a1a1aa` | ≥ 3:1; pair with text if status |
| `border/subtle` | Structural line | `#e4e4e7` | `#27272a` | Cards, dividers |

### Charts (Okabe–Ito–derived — color-blind safe)

| `charts/1` | `#0072b2` | Blue |

Always encode series with **color + label/pattern**, never hue alone.

### Badge / pill tones

`zinc` | `orange` | `emerald` | `rose` | `blue` | `amber` — soft filled pills with matching border; map to status semantics.

## Baseline / Cursor build prompt
This UI is for Web Application (responsive) — design all screens for desktop-first browser conventions with responsive breakpoints. Use pointer-first navigation, persistent collapsible left sidebar, and a slim top bar (breadcrumb/title left, search + user menu right). Content sits in a max-w-7xl container, never edge-to-edge text.

LOCKED DESIGN SYSTEM (apply to all screens):
- Color: Neutral base zinc/slate. Light bg #FFFFFF, dark bg #09090B. Surfaces use bg-card with a 1px hairline border (border-border). Accent: indigo/violet hsl(243 75% 59%) for primary actions, active nav, focus rings, and key metrics only. No rainbow palettes or gradients.
- Typography: Inter or Geist. Page title: text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight. Section: text-base or text-lg font-medium. Body: text-sm. Meta/labels: text-xs text-muted-foreground uppercase tracking-wide.
- Spacing: 8px scale. Page padding p-6→p-8, card padding p-4→p-6, grid gap-4/gap-6.
- Radius: rounded-lg for cards/inputs, rounded-md for buttons, rounded-full for avatars/pills.
- Elevation: flat by default; shadow-sm on cards, shadow-md only for dialogs/popovers.
- Components: Use shadcn/ui (New York) + lucide-react. Button, Card, Table, Badge, Tabs, Dialog, Sheet, Select, Input, DropdownMenu, Skeleton, Alert, Avatar, Tooltip, Command, Separator. Data tables: hairline row dividers, sticky headers, comfortable row height, no zebra stripes.
- App shell: persistent collapsible left sidebar (icon + label, active item uses accent) + slim top bar (breadcrumb/title left, search + user menu right).
- Motion: subtle only — 150-200ms ease transitions on hover/expand. No bouncy or flashy animation.
- States: empty (friendly illustration/icon + primary CTA), loading (Skeleton placeholders), error (Alert), permission_denied and plan_limit (distinct on-system messaging).
- Accessibility: WCAG AA contrast, visible focus-visible rings, full keyboard navigation.

Build a working Next.js (App Router) app with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and shadcn/ui. Use realistic sample data for every field from the Page by Page Data Points. Implement every page and modal from the page list, with all documented filters, status variants, and edge cases. Use the following layout and navigation:

1. App Shell:
   - Persistent collapsible left sidebar with icons + labels for: Dashboard, Briefs, Doctors, Matching, Outreach, Follow-Ups, Reporting, Admin (role-aware; hide if not permitted).
   - Slim top bar: left = breadcrumb + page title; right = search (Command), notifications (Sheet/Drawer), user menu (DropdownMenu with profile, settings, logout).
   - Main content: max-w-7xl mx-auto, p-8 on desktop, p-4 on mobile/tablet.

2. Pages (implement all, with routes, layouts, and components):
   - /login: Modern minimal login form (email, password, show/hide, forgot password). Error, loading, plan_limit, and permission_denied states.
   - /login/reset: Password reset request modal (email input, submit/cancel, error/loading/plan_limit/permission_denied states).
   - /login/reset/confirm: Set new password modal (new/confirm, requirements tooltip, error/loading/plan_limit/permission_denied states).
   - /forbidden: Permission denied screen (headline, description, return to dashboard, contact support, error/plan_limit/loading states).
   - /dashboard: Recruiter dashboard with widgets: assigned briefs, open tasks, notifications, recent activity, quick links. Filters (reporting dashboard filters), CSV export (role-restricted). All status variants: empty (illustration + CTA), loading (Skeletons), error (Alert + retry), plan_limit (banner), permission_denied (message).
   - /dashboard/notifications: Notification drawer (Sheet) with filters (type, unread only), notification list (type badge, timestamp, content, mark as read, go to related item, unread indicator), empty/loading/error/plan_limit/permission_denied states.
   - /briefs: Client brief list (Table) with filters (search, status, assigned recruiter, date created), columns (title, client, status badge, assigned recruiter, date, open positions, AI match confidence, AHPRA verification status, quick actions, pagination). All status variants: empty (illustration + create new), loading (Skeleton), error (Alert + retry), plan_limit, permission_denied.
   - /briefs/:id: Brief detail (Tabs: Details, Candidates, Timeline). Header: title, client, location, specialty, status, assigned recruiter, open positions, created date. Panels: notes, edit/delete actions, AI-powered candidate match list (with status, assignment, AI-extracted indicator, original CV, AHPRA fields), follow-up task list, add follow-up, activity timeline. All status variants: loading (Skeletons), empty (no candidates/timeline, add candidate/follow-up), error (Alert + retry), plan_limit, permission_denied.

title: Make memory_extract fully async — eliminate double timeout
content:
## Problem

`memory_extract` has a **double timeout** that causes data loss:

1. **External**: MCP gateway (30s) — kills the HTTP connection to memory-store-mcp
2. **Internal**: `generateTimeout = 120s` in `llm.go` — HTTP client timeout for Ollama call

Both are synchronous — `ExtractAndSave` calls `ExtractFacts` → `generateAnswer`, blocking the MCP handler. When text is long (e.g. full session conversation), the local qwen2.5-coder:7b on CPU (24 cores at 100%) can't finish in time, and facts are lost.

## Solution

Make `memory_extract` fully asynchronous:

- **MCP handler**: accepts text, pushes to worker queue, immediately returns `{status: "accepted"}`
- **Background worker**: calls `ExtractFacts` + `AsyncSave` with **no timeout limit**
- **Max 1 concurrent worker** — qwen2.5-coder:7b uses all 24 CPU cores at 100%
- **Optional**: job status endpoint (pending/done/failed)

## Changes needed

- `async.go` — new `AsyncExtractWorker` (job queue, 1 worker, sequential)
- `tools_extract.go` — `memory_extract` doesn't wait for result, pushes job
- `llm.go` — separate HTTP client for background calls without timeout; `--extract-model` flag for model selection

## Model note

Current model: `qwen2.5-coder:7b`. Do NOT swap without testing. Add `--extract-model` flag to allow testing `phi4-mini` vs `qwen2.5-coder:7b` on extraction quality.

## Context

Discovered during session 2026-07-08. Goal: `goal/2026-07-08/1783540135562734556`

title: feat(trello): identify every Symphony-authored comment
content:
## Problem

Symphony-created Trello comments are not identified consistently. The managed stale-blocker status now has a readable `Managed by Symphony` footer, while workpads, handoff comments, prerequisite statuses, blocker comments, and other comments may look the same as comments written by a person.

This makes it unnecessarily difficult for a board user to tell which statements came from a human and which were generated or maintained by Symphony. It also encourages each managed-comment family to invent its own attribution and recognition rules.

## Area

Trello comment UX and managed-comment ownership.

## Desired behavior

Add a consistent, human-readable `Managed by Symphony` footer to every comment that Symphony creates or owns.

The footer should make authorship clear without exposing raw machine markers. It should apply to all Symphony-owned comment paths, including at least:

- Codex workpads created or updated through Symphony's scoped tools;
- stale-blocker checking and resumed statuses;
- prerequisite and dependency statuses;
- pickup, progress, blocked, review, merge, and completion handoff comments created through Symphony tools;
- comments created directly by application-owned lifecycle or setup logic;
- any future managed-comment family.

Ordinary comments written by a user must remain unchanged. Symphony must not classify a comment as managed merely because it was posted through the same Trello account or contains similar prose.

## Ownership and safety contract

- Define one shared contributor-facing footer format and one shared parsing/formatting boundary.
- Preserve any extra identity needed by a specific managed family, such as the stale-blocker footer's link to the exact blocker comment.
- A generic footer must not make unrelated Symphony comments editable or deletable by the wrong tool. Each mutation path must still prove that the comment belongs to its own managed family before updating or deleting it.
- Visually similar, malformed, user-authored, legacy, other-card, and wrong-family comments must remain ordinary and must never be edited or deleted accidentally.
- Existing managed comments should gain the footer when their owning tool next updates them. Do not bulk-rewrite all historical card comments without a separate explicit migration decision.
- Repeated updates must produce exactly one canonical footer rather than appending duplicates.
- Trello Markdown rendering must show readable attribution and no raw HTML or opaque marker text.
- Footer text, links, and identifiers must not expose credentials, private paths, account names, or private operational context.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every current production path that creates a Symphony-owned Trello comment is inventoried and covered.
- [ ] All newly created Symphony-owned comments end with the canonical readable footer.
- [ ] Updating a managed comment preserves exactly one footer and does not duplicate it.
- [ ] Existing comments receive the footer only when their owning path legitimately updates them; unrelated historical comments remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
- [ ] Ordinary human comments never receive the footer automatically and are never reclassified based only on author account or similar text.
- [ ] Each tool can update or delete only its own managed-comment family even though all families share visible attribution.
- [ ] Stale-blocker comments retain their exact link to the blocker comment and their action-bound safety checks.
- [ ] Workpad, prerequisite, handoff, blocker, review, merge, completion, and other managed families have positive and negative ownership tests.
- [ ] Tests cover malformed footers, duplicate footers, legacy comments, copied footer text, wrong-card links, wrong-family comments, missing action IDs, retries, and duplicate cleanup.
- [ ] Generated workflows, bundled skills, README, specification, ADRs, and live-E2E guidance use the same attribution contract.
- [ ] A real disposable Trello-board verification confirms that every exercised Symphony comment renders the readable footer and that user comments remain visually and textually unchanged.

## Implementation guidance

Prefer a small shared formatter/parser or value representation used by existing comment-producing paths. Do not add a general Markdown framework, persistence subsystem, migration engine, or new provider abstraction solely for this change.

Search every caller and sink of Trello comment creation, update, duplicate classification, and deletion. Validation must occur before mutation, and failed cleanup must remain truthful and best effort.

## Compatibility

This is intended as an additive, compatible UX and ownership improvement. If adding the footer changes a documented machine-readable comment contract, identify that contract explicitly and provide narrowly scoped compatibility handling rather than treating arbitrary old text as managed indefinitely.

## Related context

- [Issue #547](https://github.com/martin-francois/symphony-trello/issues/547) and [PR #560](https://github.com/martin-francois/symphony-trello/pull/560) established the readable managed footer for stale-blocker recheck comments.

## AI Assistance (if used)

- [x] AI-assisted issue
- [x] I confirm I understand and reviewed this request

title: [SCA] Add structural clone detection and reduce detected duplication
content:
## Problem

The repository already runs PMD's Copy/Paste Detector (CPD) as part of
`./mvnw -q spotless:check verify`. CPD keeps exact and token-level copy/paste duplication from
growing, but it is not intended to find every renamed, reordered, structurally similar, or more
heavily modified clone. Those harder clone families can leave behavior and test setup implemented in
several places even while the CPD baseline remains clean.

We need a complementary Java clone detector, a reviewed baseline of its findings, and focused
refactoring of genuine duplication. The objective is less duplicated behavior and maintenance work,
not merely another green CI job.

## Area

Other — static analysis and maintainability.

## Describe the solution you want

Evaluate and integrate one reproducible clone detector that complements CPD, then use its findings to
reduce justified duplication in production and test code.

### 1. Try StoneDetector first

Use [StoneDetector](https://github.com/StoneDetector/StoneDetector) first through its published
[`stonedetector/stonedetector` Docker image](https://hub.docker.com/r/stonedetector/stonedetector).
The current research comparison reports competitive exact/near-miss performance, high precision,
and the best recall among the compared tools for Strongly and Moderately Type-3 clones in its
BigCloneEval results. That harder Type-3 coverage is the main reason to prefer it over adding another
token-only detector. See the
[StoneDetector evaluation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03435) and
[BigCloneEval](https://github.com/jeffsvajlenko/BigCloneEval).

Do not use a floating `latest` image in committed automation. Resolve an reviewed image version or
immutable digest, record the upstream source revision and license, and pin the exact digest. Provide
a repository-owned wrapper command so local and CI runs use the same paths, configuration, limits,
and output normalization.

Run the container with:

- the Java source trees mounted read-only;
- no credentials or unrelated host paths;
- networking disabled during analysis;
- no privileged mode, added capabilities, or Docker socket mount;
- a disposable writable output directory;
- explicit CPU, memory, and timeout expectations; and
- deterministic, repository-relative result paths that do not expose private host paths.

Scan both `src/main/java` and `src/test/java`, and report whether a finding is production-production,
test-test, or production-test. Measure the default/recommended configuration first, then tune only
with documented evidence. Record parsing errors and prove that every intended Java file was analyzed;
a zero-finding report is invalid if Java 25 syntax or another parser limitation silently skipped
files.

StoneDetector is suitable only if it:

- parses the repository's current Java sources without silent omissions;
- produces repeatable results for the same commit and configuration;
- finds useful clone families beyond the existing CPD report;
- has an acceptable false-positive rate after narrow tuning;
- fits a documented local and hosted-CI runtime and memory budget; and
- can be used reproducibly and safely under its license and pinned supply-chain inputs.

### 2. Fall back to NIL if StoneDetector is not workable

If StoneDetector fails any suitability condition, document the exact evidence and evaluate
[NIL](https://github.com/kusumotolab/NIL) next. NIL is an MIT-licensed detector for scalable,
large-variance clones using N-grams, an inverted index, and LCS, and it is one of the strongest
follow-up candidates compared in the StoneDetector evaluation.

Pin a reviewed NIL release or commit and every downloaded artifact checksum. Run it in an isolated,
reproducible container built from repository-controlled configuration rather than installing an
unpinned tool into the runner. Apply the same complete-input, deterministic-output, resource,
security, and no-silent-skip criteria used for StoneDetector.

Do not keep both new detectors merely because both can run. Select the first suitable high-signal
detector, record why it was selected, and avoid two overlapping gates with different baselines.

If neither detector can analyze the project reliably, do not add a misleading passing check. Record
the attempted versions, commands, failures, and the smallest remaining dependency in this issue or a
focused follow-up.

### 3. Review and reduce the baseline

For every reported clone family:

1. Compare it with `target/cpd.xml` and identify whether the new detector adds signal beyond CPD.
2. Inspect the full methods and their callers rather than refactoring only the reported line ranges.
3. Fix justified duplication with a shared production abstraction, existing domain type, focused
   helper, parameterized test, fixture, or assertion utility when that improves the design.
4. Keep independently meaningful behavior separate. Similar-looking code is not automatically the
   same contract, and test readability must not be traded for an overly generic fixture.
5. Prove behavior before and after each substantive refactoring with focused unit or integration
   tests. A later cleanup commit must not silently repair an earlier incomplete refactoring.
6. Tune the detector only for a repeatable false-positive category. Every exclusion or accepted
   baseline entry needs a narrow scope, owner-facing explanation, and regression evidence showing
   why duplication is clearer than abstraction.

Group changes into cohesive clone families so reviews can verify that each extraction preserves
behavior. A large cleanup is acceptable when every change is justified, but unrelated redesign or
formatting does not belong in the same pull request.

### 4. Make the selected detector durable in CI

Start with a report-only run while the baseline is being classified. Once justified findings are
fixed and false positives are narrowly documented, make the selected detector blocking for relevant
Java changes.

The final integration must:

- expose one documented local command and run the exact same wrapper in CI;
- keep the existing PMD CPD gate enabled because it provides a faster complementary boundary;
- pin the detector image/artifacts and configuration;
- fail on detector errors, timeouts, parse omissions, malformed output, and new unaccepted clones;
- distinguish "no clones" from "analysis did not complete";
- produce a concise artifact or annotation with both clone locations and enough context to review;
- avoid privileged workflows, secrets, and `pull_request_target` execution of pull-request code;
- cache safely or use Java path filters where practical so the large image does not waste resources
  on documentation-only changes; and
- include the pinned dependency in Renovate or an equivalent explicit update process.

Update `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `docs/agents/static-analysis.md`, and the accepted static-analysis ADR (or
add a superseding ADR if the decision changes materially) with the selected tool, command,
configuration rationale, triage order, suppression/baseline policy, resource cost, and relationship
to CPD.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A before-change report captures the selected detector, immutable version/digest, exact command,
      configuration, runtime, peak memory, input-file count, parse/error count, and normalized clone
      families for production and tests.
- [ ] StoneDetector is evaluated first with its pinned Docker image. If it is rejected, the issue or
      ADR contains concrete suitability evidence before NIL is evaluated.
- [ ] If NIL is selected, its source revision/artifact checksum and reproducible container build are
      pinned and documented.
- [ ] The selected detector finds meaningful near-miss or structural duplication beyond PMD CPD, or
      the work stops truthfully instead of adding a redundant gate.
- [ ] Every finding is classified as fixed, narrowly accepted with rationale, or false positive with
      evidence; high finding counts are not dismissed as noise.
- [ ] Justified production and test duplication is materially reduced without weakening behavior,
      assertions, or coverage.
- [ ] Before/after reports demonstrate the reduction and focused tests prove each refactored clone
      family's behavior remains intact.
- [ ] A repository-owned wrapper produces deterministic results locally and in CI, including failure
      tests for timeout, parser omission, malformed output, and detector failure.
- [ ] The final CI job is blocking only after baseline cleanup, runs only in a safe unprivileged
      context, and retains the existing blocking PMD CPD check.
- [ ] `./mvnw -q pmd:cpd` and `./mvnw -q spotless:check verify` remain green.
- [ ] Documentation and ADRs explain the chosen detector, rejected alternative, operating cost,
      update process, and the distinct clone types covered by CPD and the new detector.

## Alternatives considered

- **Use PMD CPD alone:** fast and already enforced, but it does not cover the harder structural and
  modified clone family this issue targets.
- **Integrate StoneDetector without cleaning findings:** produces a dashboard but leaves the actual
  maintenance problem unresolved.
- **Add StoneDetector and NIL together:** increases CI cost and triage duplication without first
  proving that one detector is insufficient.
- **Fail CI immediately on the first report:** encourages broad exclusions or an opaque baseline
  before findings have been reviewed.
- **Use an AI-only similarity review:** not deterministic enough for a blocking local and CI gate.

## Current workaround

PMD CPD blocks token-level duplication, while reviewers and contributors must notice more heavily
modified or structurally similar implementations by hand.

## Affects existing users?

No user-facing contract change. This changes repository maintenance and CI only. Refactorings made
from detector findings must preserve existing behavior and remain covered by tests.

## Additional context

Related completed work:

- [Issue #78](https://github.com/martin-francois/symphony-trello/issues/78) introduced the curated PMD
  and CPD rollout.
- [Issue #128](https://github.com/martin-francois/symphony-trello/issues/128) cleaned the original CPD
  baseline and made CPD blocking.
- [ADR 0039](https://github.com/martin-francois/symphony-trello/blob/main/docs/adr/0039-curated-pmd-rules-and-cpd-baseline.md)
  records the current CPD decision.

title: Azure OpenAI Responses (store:false) still 400s on multi-turn reasoning replay in 0.80.3 (bare rs_ id, no encrypted_content backfill)
content:
### What happened?

Multi-turn conversations against `azure-openai-responses` reasoning models fail on the follow-up turn with:

```
400 Item with id 'rs_...' not found. Items are not persisted when store is set to false.
Try again with store set to true, or remove this item from your input.
```

This is the same class of failure as #4272 (Azure; closed as `closed-because-bigrefactor`, with fix PR #4256 never merged) and the OpenAI-side #3369 / #5059. It **still reproduces on 0.80.3 / current main** — the refactor did not close the Azure path.

**Root cause (code-grounded, 0.80.3):**

`packages/ai/src/api/openai-responses-shared.ts` → `convertResponsesMessages()` replays the captured reasoning item verbatim, including its server-side `rs_` id:

```js
if (block.type === "thinking") {
    if (block.thinkingSignature) {
        const reasoningItem = JSON.parse(block.thinkingSignature);
        output.push(reasoningItem); // keeps the original rs_... id
    }
}
```

`packages/ai/src/api/azure-openai-responses.ts` sends `store: false`, and requests `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]` **only** when a reasoning effort/summary is set; there is **no backfill** of `encrypted_content` from the final `response.completed.response.output[]`.

When the captured reasoning item ends up without `encrypted_content` (per #4272, Azure does not always populate it on the intermediate `response.output_item.done`), the next turn's `input` carries a **bare `rs_` id**. Under `store: false` the server persists nothing, so the lookup fails → 400.

The tool-call path has the same shape: the `fc_` item id is omitted only for cross-model replay (`isDifferentModel`), not for same-model Azure under `store: false`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure `azure-openai-responses/<reasoning model>` (e.g. `gpt-5-mini`) with a reasoning effort set.
2. Turn 1: a normal assistant turn that produces a reasoning (`thinking`) block (optionally followed by a tool call + tool result).
3. Turn 2: send another message in the same session; `convertResponsesMessages()` replays the prior reasoning item into `input`.
4. Azure returns the 400 above.

### Expected behavior

Turn 2 succeeds. Under `store: false` the converter must not replay a reasoning item that references non-persisted server state. Either:

- **backfill** `encrypted_content` from `response.completed.response.output[]` into the captured `thinkingSignature`, so the replayed item is a valid stateless payload (the #4256 approach, preserves reasoning continuity); or
- for `api === "azure-openai-responses"`, **drop** reasoning items that have no `encrypted_content`, and **strip** the `rs_`/`fc_` server ids from the items it does replay (encrypted_content is the stateless carrier).

The OpenAI / OpenAI-Codex / OpenCode Responses paths should stay unchanged.

### Version

0.80.3 (also reproduces on current main). Related prior reports: #4272, #4256, #3369, #5059, #6023.

title: DevBox-native unattended Codex auto-runner foundation
content:
Tracks the workflow/tooling foundation and finished end state for a Settleora DevBox-native unattended Codex auto-runner.

Current status as of task `20260712-1821`: keep open. #880 is accepted and closed, so monitoring, incident/recovery notification, activity notification, dedupe, idle silence, Windows-off operation, and rollback evidence are complete. The remaining #800 work is serious autonomous-loop capability, not monitoring.

Important correction: current restrictive defaults and low-risk canary behavior are staged scaffolding, not the final design. The earlier wording that real unattended mutation and auto-merge remain disabled/gated describes the historical foundation state, not the final #800 requirement.

Authoritative finished target A-H:

A. Autonomous work across normal development domains: workflow/tooling, docs/planning, mobile/web/admin UI, API/domain runtime, auth/session/security, storage/file privacy/authz, money/settlement/payment, schema/migrations, OpenAPI/generated clients, sync/import/export/restore, Docker/CI/deployment, and other normal Settleora domains. Sensitive work should run automatically when requirements and architecture are complete and no genuine human decision is needed, with stronger contracts and gates, but current repository manual gates remain authoritative until a reviewed policy PR explicitly narrows or reclassifies them.

B. Real feature-bundle execution: one feature-bundle branch, two to four related implementation sub-slices, checkpoint validation, persistent bundle state/reports, recovery/continuation, one final validation, mandatory reviews, one PR, CI, and conditional auto-merge. Split focused branches for auth/security, storage/privacy/authz, money/settlement, schema/migrations, OpenAPI/generated clients plus large runtime/UI, Docker/CI/deployment, uncertain architecture, and hard cross-domain work.

C. Automatic high-quality issue creation: after planning/design merges and during implementation/review/CI/acceptance, derive linked runnable implementation/fix/blocker/follow-up/future-gate issues with duplicate search across issues, PRs, comments, reports, and ledger. Generated issues must include full planning metadata, guardrails, allowed paths, validation, reviewer routing, manual decisions if any, acceptance, close rule, and machine-readable contract.

D. Automatic issue completion and progress hygiene: after merge, close narrow clearly complete issues, comment with PR/head/merge/validation/review evidence, remove transient labels, update project/status/progress where safe, update the ledger and parent umbrellas, and keep ambiguous umbrellas open.

E. Mandatory independent external review: every auto-merged PR requires independent external review, Codex mechanics/security review, local validation, GitHub CI/security checks, and exact-head verification. Routine work routes cheap; sensitive/high-risk routes strong; very large/cross-domain splits or escalates; disagreement routes tie-breaker or human escalation. Missing/unavailable/failed/malformed/stale/mismatched-SHA review blocks merge.

F. Automatic merge across approved domains: auto-merge must not remain permanently limited to low-risk canaries. PRs may auto-merge, including sensitive-domain code PRs, when requirements/architecture are clear, no manual decision/action is required, scope/validation/reviews/CI/security/exact-head gates pass, and no stop condition exists. Production deployment and other explicit manual actions remain separate.

G. title: 定时调用凭证：补齐 agent key 双轨撤销、失败补偿与 allowlist fail-closed
content:
## 背景

对 milestone 33（Scheduled Agent-Key Credential v1）在 commit `34f336bd8f43adbd04714261105d2750c96c160a` 做验收复查后，确认核心链路已经实现：NyxID `full_key` 写入 Garnet secret vault，actor state / projection 只保存 `SecretReference`，执行时再现场解密。

但 #2689 / #2690 约定的密钥生命周期闭环仍有可达缺口。当前 `dotnet test aevatar.slnx --nologo --no-restore` 和 `bash tools/ci/architecture_guards.sh` 均通过，因此这些问题需要新增行为测试才能被门禁捕获。

关联：#2404、#2689、#2690。

## 已确认问题

### 1. vault `PutAsync` 失败后不会撤销已铸造的 NyxID key

`ScheduledAgentCreatorTool` 先调用 `IssueAsync`，再直接调用 mapper；`MapAsync` 内执行 vault `PutAsync`，但调用点没有异常补偿。若 Garnet 写入抛异常，NyxID key 会成为孤儿。

- `agents/Aevatar.GAgents.Authoring.Lark/ScheduledAgentCreatorTool.cs:185-193`
- `agents/Aevatar.GAgents.Authoring.Lark/ScheduledAgentCreateRequestMapper.cs:194-204`

### 2. vault 写入成功但 actor 初始化失败时，只撤销 NyxID key

initialize catch 只调用 `TryRevokeAsync(token, apiKeyId)`；已经写入的 vault reference 没有执行 `ISecretVault.RevokeAsync`，加密记录仍可解析直到过期或人工清理。

- `agents/Aevatar.GAgents.Authoring.Lark/ScheduledAgentCreatorTool.cs:196-204`

### 3. 删除 scheduled agent 时没有执行双轨撤销

删除流程 tombstone 后仅调用 NyxID DELETE/outbox。catalog revocation 事实中已经携带 `NyxApiKeyReference`，但删除链路没有消费该 reference 执行本地 vault revoke。

- `agents/Aevatar.GAgents.Authoring.Lark/AgentBuilderTool.cs:261-281`
- `agents/Aevatar.GAgents.Scheduled/UserAgentCatalogGAgent.cs:418-429`

### 4. 出站 allowlist 派生失败时仍 fail-open

owner LLM config 查询异常后，issuer 返回 `null` 并继续铸造不含 LLM route grant 的 key，让失败延迟到定时运行时 403；这与 #2690 的“出站面无法解析时 fail closed 拒绝铸 key”不一致。

- `agents/Aevatar.GAgents.Authoring.Lark/ScheduledAgentApiKeyIssuer.cs:206-223`

### 5. raw key holder 仍是可公开读取的 record string 属性

`ScheduledAgentApiKeyIssueResult.FullKey` 已有 `[JsonIgnore]` 且 `ToString()` 打码，但仍是公开 record 属性，不满足 #2690 约定的不可序列化 opaque holder；其他 serializer、反射、record copy/deconstruction 仍可传播该值。

- `agents/Aevatar.GAgents.Scheduled/ScheduledAgentApiKeyIssueResult.cs:6-51`

## 范围

1. 将 mint -> vault put -> actor initialize 收敛到一个窄的 provisioning 生命周期编排，显式持有补偿所需的 `apiKeyId + SecretReference`。
2. 任一步失败时执行双轨补偿：
   - 已产生 vault reference：立即、幂等调用 `ISecretVault.RevokeAsync`。
   - 已产生 NyxID key：尝试 DELETE；无法完成时写入既有 durable revocation outbox，禁止静默丢弃。
3. agent 删除与后续 key replacement/rotation 复用同一撤销语义：vault revoke 与 NyxID revoke/outbox 都必须可重试、幂等并可观察。
4. owner LLM route/出站面解析异常时 fail closed，并确保调用 NyxID create-key 前返回明确错误。
5. 用不可序列化、`ToString()` 永久打码的 opaque secret holder 替代公开 `string FullKey`；raw key 只存在于 provisioning 调用栈。
6. 仅使用 NyxID 现有公开 API，不要求修改 NyxID 仓库。

## 验收标准

- [ ] vault `PutAsync` 抛异常：NyxID DELETE 被调用；失败时产生可重放 outbox。
- [ ] vault 写入成功、mapper/actor initialize 失败：同一 reference 被 vault revoke，NyxID DELETE 被调用或进入 outbox。
- [ ] 删除 agent：使用 catalog 中的 exact `ref / purpose / ownerScopeKey / apiKeyId` 撤销 vault；下一次 `ResolveAsync` 必须失败；NyxID revoke/outbox 同时发生。
- [ ] 重复删除、重复补偿和 outbox replay 均幂等，不会复活 key 或丢失 pending revocation。
- [ ] owner LLM config/outbound surface 查询失败：不调用 NyxID create-key，返回 fail-closed 错误。
- [ ] raw key 不进入 JSON、Protobuf state/event/readmodel、日志或错误返回；holder 的结构化日志与 `ToString()` 始终打码。
- [ ] 新增针对上述每条失败分支的确定性测试，不使用轮询延时。
- [ ] `dotnet test aevatar.slnx --nologo` 通过。
- [ ] `bash tools/ci/architecture_guards.sh` 与 `bash tools/ci/test_stability_guards.sh` 通过。

## 发布门槛

该 issue 是 scheduled agent durable key 生命周期闭环的发布 blocker。仅“密文驻库 + 执行时解密”通过不能替代创建失败补偿和删除双轨撤销。

title: 🎯 EPIC · Матрица [83 формата × {SW-bitexact / decode-HW / compute-HW}] на AX7203
content:
## 🎯 ЭПИК: Прошить полный каталог — матрица [83 формата × {SW-bitexact / decode-HW / compute-HW}]

**Цель:** довести каталог GoldenFloat до полного аппаратного conformance на FPGA **AX7203** (XC7A200T-2, `xc7a200tfbg484-2`, IDCODE `0x13636093`).

**Якоря:** arXiv:2606.05017 (GoldenFloat φ-derived FP), arXiv:2606.09686 (каталог + bit-exact conformance, **erratum: 83 формата**, не 84).

---

### 🔄 Сессия 2026-07-02/03: **Tier-E 53 → 71/83** (+18 ячеек)

**6 HW-proven track-b ячеек** (sim 64/64 → CI synth → flash → UART → Tier-E на этом #199):
1. **decimal64** (IEEE 754 BID, table+multiply, 288-bit) — commit `b857e55f1`
2. **decimal32** (BID, 240-bit) — commit `2b28e146c`
3. **double_double** (Bailey/Hida 2×FP64, FP-add→FP32) — commit `62a9fec45`
4. **takum16** (Hunhold 2024 logarithmic, BRAM-LUT 65536-entry) — commit `fdb9ff439`
5. **quad_double** (4×FP64, FP-add→FP32) — commit `b4a5647d6`
6. **decimal128** (BID, 336-bit) — commit `af40c275f`

**4 доказанных шаблона** (переиспользуемы):
1. **Algebraic table+multiply** (decimal 10^de, eliminates divide, G=210 guard bits).
2. **FP-add→FP32** (align mant53 → signed accumulate → normalize → round 24-bit).
3. **BRAM-LUT** (precompute offline → $readmemh → trivial routing).
4. **Transcendental exp-via-tables** (2^L decomposition + BRAM table + quadratic Taylor + subnormal rounding).

**Decode rigor-close (+12):** 8 ранних P0 декодеров (int4, fp4_e2m1, fp6_e2m3, fp6_e3m2, fp8_e5m2, lns8, tf32, binary16) через `corona_decode_host --fmt N` + 4 host-5 (bf16, int8, nf4, posit8) через новые CI workflows (commit `55165e6d9`).

**Compute-30 audit (+10 re-flashed):** gf4/6/8/12/16/20/24-add + gf6/8/20-mul — индивидуальные Tier-E proofs (previously batch-only).

---

### Честная матрица прогресса (2026-07-03, обновлено сессией)

| Столбец | Состояние | Тег |
|---------|-----------|-----|
| **SW-bitexact** (внешний оракул) | **69 / 83** | [t27 merge wave: #1235/#1229/#1231/#1233 merged] |
| SW structural (нет числовых векторов) | 14 / 83 | [открытая задача — нужен oracle/spec per format] |
| **decode-HW** (AX7203, Tier-E) | **41 / 83** | [измерено на железе; sim→CI→flash→UART→proof на #199] |
| **compute-HW** (bit-exact) | **30 / 83** | [ADD 10/10 + MUL 10/10 + SUB 10/10, GF4–GF32] |
| **ИТОГО Tier E (HW)** | **71 / 83** (85.5%) | [полная цепь: CI run + SHA + UART на #199; ноль Тир C] |

> **decode-HW 41/83** включает: bf16, int8, nf4, fp8_e4m3, fp8_e5m2, posit8, fp4_e2m1, int4, fp6_e2m3, fp6_e3m2, lns8, tf32, binary16, e8m0 (оригинальные 14) + bcd, bitnet, mxfp8_e4m3, mxint8 (Phase B 4) + int16, posit16, gf14, gf10, lns16, takum8, binary32, int32, posit32, ibm_hfp32, vax_f, ms_mbf32, binary64, vax_d (vintage 11) + vax_g, ibm_hfp64, binary128, ms_mbf64 (2026-07 vintage 4) + decimal64, decimal32, double_double, takum16, quad_double, decimal128 (track-b 6).

> **takum32/64 routing = FAILED on Artix-7 200T (XC7A200T)** (CI runs 28675516786/28675516794, 2026-07-03; both synthesize via yosys but all 8 nextpnr seeds timed out unrouted, 30min/seed inner-SIGKILL timeout worked as designed). takum = **NOT Tier E** per rule #1. ~10 structural форматов — **математически недостижимы** (нет single-value decode law: block_fp, shared_exp, per_channel_scale, stochastic_rounding, gf256, minifloat, q_format, etc.).

> **83/83 HW математически невозможно** — ~10 structural форматов не имеют decode law (контейнеры/масштабы/режимы, не числа). **Achievable HW ceiling = 71/83 на AX7203** (takum32/64 routing falsified by CI; see comment issuecomment-4880596167).

---

## 🎯 Achievable HW ceiling = 71/83 on AX7203 (canonical — why 83/83 is mathematically impossible, and why 73 was NOT reached)

**Зафиксировано 2026-07-03.** Это закрывает вопрос «почему не 83» раз и навсегда.
83/83 HW-decode **математически невозможно** — ~10 форматов являются
структурными (контейнеры/масштабы/режимы/поля), а не числами, и не имеют
**single-value decode law**: битовый паттерн НЕ отображается однозначно в одно
real-число без внешнего контекста. HW-decode для них не определён математически,
а не инженерно — никакой синтез/маршрутизация/ресурс это не исправит.

**Achievable HW ceiling = 71/83 на AX7203** = 83 − 10 structural − 2 unroutable (takum32, takum64: synthesize via yosys но do **not** route on Artix-7 200T (XC7A200T) — CI 28675516786/794, all 8 seeds timed out 2026-07-03; despite optimizations `-flatten` removal `d08d9878b`, datapath 119+140→94+72-bit `b537d0336`, seed widening `561e452cf`, subnormal fix `399bb0cf8`). **Выше на ЭТОМ кристалле — некуда.** 73+ требует большую density part или принципиально иной datapath → новый investigation, не продолжение.

### Structural formats (~10) — математическое обоснование каждого

| Формат | Класс | Почему HW-decode не определён |
|--------|-------|-------------------------------|
| `block_fp` | контейнер | блок mantiss разделяет **один block-exponent**;单个 элемент без block-context не имеет значения — decode требует внешний масштаб |
| `shared_exp` | контейнер | N mantiss + 1 общий exponent; элемент undefined в isolation (метаданные блока) |
| `per_channel_scale` | квантование | raw int + внешний per-channel scale-factor; значение = int × scale, где scale — отдельные данные модели, не битовый паттерн |
| `stochastic_rounding` | режим | это **режим округления**, не кодирование; нет битового паттерна для decode (свойство операции конверсии) |
| `gf256` | поле Галуа | GF(2⁸) — 256 элементов поля с примитивным полиномом 0x11D; элементы {0..255} — **полевые элементы, не real-числа**; нет естественного отображения в FP32 (проверено: t27 `.trinity/seals/triformat-gf256.json` подтверждает) |
| `minifloat` | параметрическое семейство | generic mini-FP без фиксированных (E,M); конкретные экземпляры (fp4_e2m1, fp6_*, fp8_*) УЖЕ decode-HW proven — сам generic-класс не имеет единой кодировки |
| `q_format` | параметрическое семейство | generic Qm.n fixed-point без фиксированных (m,n); конкретный экземпляр decodable (value = bits/2ⁿ), но generic — контейнер |
| `tapered_fp` | параметрическое семейство | generic tapered-precision; конкретные экземпляры (posit8/16/32) УЖЕ decode-HW proven — generic-класс не имеет единой кодировки |
| `mxfp` (generic) | контейнер | microscaling-контейнер: mantiss + shared block-scale; элемент undefined в isolation (как block_fp). Конкретные mxfp8_e4m3/mxint8 — proven |
| `block_minifloat` | контейнер | block-scaled minifloat — комбинация block_fp + minifloat; та же проблема внешнего block-context |

**Общий принцип:** формат имеет HW decode law ⇔ существует инъективное отображение
битовый-паттерн → real-число (FP32), определяемое ТОЛЬКО самим битовым паттерном.
Контейнеры/режимы/параметрические-семейства/поля этот критерий не проходят — им
нужен внешний контекст (block, channel, параметр, или алгебра без real-значения).

> **Для будущих агентов/loop'ов:** НЕ пытаться прошить эти ~10 structural форматов на HW —
> это не инженерная задача, а математическая невозможность. И НЕ пытаться повторно
> прошить takum32/64 на Artix-7 200T (XC7A200T) — они synthesize но не route (CI 28675516786/794
> falsified, 2026-07-03; все оптимизации перепробованы). Цель EPIC на ЭТОМ кристалле =
> **71/83** (TERMINAL — достигнут). 73+ = новый investigation (большая part / иной
> datapath), не продолжение этого epic. Финальный прогресс: Tier-E **71/83 = потолок**.


---

### Инфраструктура
- **Board:** AX7203 XC7A200T-2FBG484I, IDCODE `0x13636093`, JTAG AL321 (FT2232H vid:0x0403 pid:0x6014), UART CP2102N `/dev/cu.usbserial-120` @160000 baud.
- **openocd cfg:** `fpga/openxc7-synth/ax7203_al321.cfg`. Flash: `sudo -n /opt/homebrew/bin/openocd -c "init" -c "pld load 0 <BIT>" -c "runtest 200000" -c "shutdown"` (~78s).
- **CI:** GitHub Actions, openXC7 Docker (`regymm/openxc7`), yosys + nextpnr-xilinx + fasm2bit. Workflows: `heap+sa x8` + `-nodsp` for large datapaths. **Key lesson: remove `-flatten` for BRAM+wide-logic designs** (yosys hangs 3h+ otherwise).
- **Catalog:** `fpga/CATALOG_MATRIX_83.md` — decode 41 / compute 30 / Tier-E 71.
- **HANDOFF:** `HANDOFF_2026_07_03.md` — comprehensive handoff for next agent (4 templates, bugs, constants, approach).

encoding ≠ compute ≠ FPGA. Все HW-цифры — измерено на AX7203 (IDCODE `0x13636093`). Tier E = CI run + битстрим SHA256 + UART-лог на этом #199.

title: `JsonSchemaTransformer` skips `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` members when the node also has a `type`
content:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I'm using the latest version of Pydantic AI (reproduced on `main` @ `3adb9b0`).
- [x] I've searched the issue tracker before opening this.

### Description

`JsonSchemaTransformer._handle` only recurses into `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` members when the node has no `type`:

```python
# pydantic_ai/_json_schema.py
elif type_ is None:
    schema = self._handle_union(schema, 'allOf')
    schema = self._handle_union(schema, 'anyOf')
    schema = self._handle_union(schema, 'oneOf')
```

`allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` are independent applicators: a node can legally carry both a `type` and one of them, and such nodes show up in practice via user-provided and MCP tool `inputSchema`s. When that happens, `_handle_object`/`_handle_array` recurse `properties`/`items` but never the composition members, so those members (and their nested subschemas) are never walked and `transform` is never applied to them. Provider transformers then leave provider-incompatible keys in place inside the members.

This is the same root family as #6394 (which added `allOf` recursion for the typeless case); it just is not reached when the node also has a `type`.

Invariant: every subschema in the tree should be visited by `transform` exactly once; `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` can co-exist with `type`.

### Minimal, Reproducible Example

Offline, no network or provider call:

```python
from pydantic_ai.profiles.google import GoogleJsonSchemaTransformer

schema = {
    'type': 'object',
    'properties': {'p': {'type': 'string'}},
    'anyOf': [
        {'type': 'integer', 'title': 'Count', 'exclusiveMinimum': 0},
    ],
}
out = GoogleJsonSchemaTransformer(schema).walk()
print(out['anyOf'][0])
# actual  : {'type': 'integer', 'title': 'Count', 'exclusiveMinimum': 0}
# expected: {'type': 'integer'}
```

`GoogleJsonSchemaTransformer.transform` strips `title` and `exclusiveMinimum` (Gemini rejects them), but because the `anyOf` member is never walked they survive and get sent to the provider. `OpenAIJsonSchemaTransformer` (strict) is affected the same way: the composition member does not get `additionalProperties: false`/`required` added. A node without the sibling `type` (e.g. `{'anyOf': [...]}`) is transformed correctly, so the miss is specific to typed + composition nodes.

### Proposed fix

Recurse the composition members in the typed case too. One design choice to flag: the typeless path uses `_handle_union`, which collapses a lone member into the parent (`handled[0] | schema`). Doing that on a typed node would merge the member into the parent and mutate it, which is the concern raised in #5417 (closed not_planned). So the safe shape is a members-only recursion that keeps the keyword in place:

```python
if type_ is None:
    schema = self._handle_union(schema, 'allOf')
    schema = self._handle_union(schema, 'anyOf')
    schema = self._handle_union(schema, 'oneOf')
else:
    for union_kind in ('allOf', 'anyOf', 'oneOf'):
        if members := schema.get(union_kind):
            schema[union_kind] = [self._handle(member) for member in members]
```

I have this change plus a regression test staged on a branch: https://github.com/ebarkhordar/pydantic-ai/tree/fix/json-schema-composition-recursion . Happy to open a PR if you want this approach, or if you would rather take it internally I can validate the fix against the repro above.

### Verification

- Reproduced on `main` @ `3adb9b0` in a clean Docker container (python:3.12-slim, `pydantic-ai-slim` installed).
- With the fix, the `GoogleJsonSchemaTransformer` repro member becomes `{'type': 'integer'}`; a control schema with no composition sibling produces byte-identical output before and after, so the common path is unchanged.
- `OpenAIJsonSchemaTransformer` on `{type: object, oneOf: [...]}`: the parent output is identical before/after; only the member additionally gets the strict-mode `additionalProperties: false`/`required` it was missing.
- Full `tests/test_json_schema.py` passes with the change (9 tests).
- Not verified: an actual live Gemini/OpenAI request rejecting the keys. This is shown via `.walk()` output, not a captured provider 400.

### Python, Pydantic AI & LLM client version

- Python: 3.12
- Pydantic AI: `main` @ `3adb9b0` (pydantic-ai-slim)
- LLM provider SDK: n/a (offline schema-transform repro)

---

Disclosure: this report and the linked branch were prepared with AI assistance. I reproduced and verified everything above myself in Docker before filing.

title: JSON-LD is injected via next/script after hydration and is absent from the exported static HTML
content:
`PageWrapper` renders structured data with `<Script id={id} type="application/ld+json" ...>` and no `strategy`, so the default `afterInteractive` applies — which renders `null` server-side and only appends the tag client-side after hydration. On this `output: "export"` site, none of the WebSite/SoftwareApplication JSON-LD exists in the served HTML (live-verified: the raw HTML of nobuddy.org pages contains no `ld+json` tag). A secondary bug: `/` and `/tools` share the same title, so PageWrapper derives the identical Script `id` for both, and next/script's module-global LoadCache then skips injecting the second page's different JSON-LD during client navigation.

**Severity:** medium — any consumer that parses raw HTML without executing JS (many crawlers, validators, social/AI scrapers) never sees the structured data; the entire purpose of PageWrapper is defeated for the static export.

**Locations:**
- `web-buddy/src/app/components/PageWrapper.tsx:23-27`
- `web-buddy/src/app/page.tsx:10` and `web-buddy/src/app/tools/page.tsx:9` (identical id inputs)

**Suggested fix:** Replace `next/script` with a plain `<script type="application/ld+json" dangerouslySetInnerHTML={...} />` in the server component (the approach Next's own JSON-LD docs recommend); that also moots the id-dedup bug. Do red/green TDD: first add a failing test asserting the built HTML for each page contains its own ld+json payload, then fix until green.

**Quality bar:** SOLID, DRY, KISS — clean, readable, well-tested code; no new errors, warnings, or test failures.

title: Morning digest delivery tracker (GitHub era)
content:
## Purpose

GitHub-era replacement for Gitea Issue #1950 (pre-flip; resolves against the Gitea cold-DR per the Gate-3 epoch ruling, #3231). This issue is the standing delivery surface for the daily morning-digest pipeline:

- `.github/workflows/morning-digest.yml` posts the LT-facing delivery comment here every morning (marker: `<!-- tbm-morning-digest-delivery date=YYYY-MM-DD -->`, edited in place on same-date reruns).
- Upstream automation publishers post marker report comments here (`<!-- morning-health-check:run -->`, `<!-- control-plane-health:run -->`, `<!-- stall-sweep-summary -->`, `<!-- education-runtime:snapshot -->`, `<!-- claude-session-audit:run -->`, `<!-- buggsy-hw-readiness:run -->`) that `generate_morning_digest.py` reads back into SOURCE FRESHNESS / TBM HEALTH WATCH.
- Digest PRs use `Refs` against this issue with `skip-issue-link` so it stays open as a standing surface.

Standing surface — never closes. Ported under Issue #569.

## Outcome Type: automation-delivery

## Build Skills

title: review hook: diff vs origin/<default> produces stale-base phantom-deletion findings on serially merged PRs
content:
## What happened

autumngarage/cortex#495 branched from main at commit `2bf1ada`. PR #494 then merged, adding `.cortex/journal/2026-06-09-pr-merged-pr493.md` and regenerating `state.md`. When #495 entered the merge gate, the review diffed the branch against `origin/main` (which now contained #494) and reported two **phantom findings**:

> - `.cortex/journal/2026-06-09-pr-merged-pr493.md:1` — deletes a tracked Journal entry, violating the append-only project-memory invariant
> - `.cortex/state.md:5` — generated state is rewound to an older HEAD/source set

Nothing was deleted or rewound — the branch simply predated #494. The reviewer correctly read the diff it was given; the diff itself was wrong for the question being asked. This is the recurring stale-base class (same shape as the sentinel #49/#50/#51 serial-merge incidents).

## Mitigation that worked

`gh api -X PUT repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/495/update-branch`, then rerun the gate → clean merge.

## Proposed fix (either layer works)

1. **Diff at the merge base**: review `git diff $(git merge-base origin/<default> HEAD)...HEAD` (triple-dot semantics) instead of `--base origin/<default>` two-dot, so already-merged sibling work never appears as deletions; or
2. **Auto-update before review**: when the branch is behind the base, call update-branch (or rebase in the worktree) before computing the review diff, failing visibly on conflicts; or at minimum
3. **Detect and instruct**: when behind-base is detected, prefix the review output with a stale-base warning and the update-branch command instead of letting phantom deletions reach the reviewer.

Serial merges of small PRs are the normal workflow under `open-pr.sh --auto-merge`; every PR after the first in a session is exposed to this class.

## Evidence

- autumngarage/cortex#495 round-1 review comment (phantom journal-deletion findings) vs its clean round-2 pass after update-branch with an otherwise unchanged diff.

title: Fix workshop landing hierarchy, coverless cards, and Mermaid layout shift
content:
# Fix workshop landing hierarchy, coverless cards, and Mermaid layout shift

Status: pending
Tags: `bug`, `P1`, `content`, `frontend`
Depends on: None
Blocks: —

## Scope

### Reporter context and current evidence

Source: feedback from Alexey and a team member on 2026-07-13, followed by a screenshot-backed designer investigation.

Alexey's original observation:

> "I don't like the workshop landing it has two columns and per our design system we should have this also it's too jumpy now for individual workshops and the banners disappeared. not sure if we need the banners but now it's just a placeholder which is worse"

The team decision on workshop covers resolves the banner question:

> "The third point is that we will not have the workshop cover images. That means the cards need to change. Right now the covers simply went away, but the card itself stayed the same, and there is just a graduation cap icon in place of the image. If there are no pictures, that icon should not be added at all."

The page-hierarchy feedback is that the landing header adds useful orientation but puts too much information in one place. The three value points may remain, but they must no longer compete with the introduction in a desktop side column.

Verified against production and `origin/main` during grooming:

- `GET /workshops` still uses the arbitrary two-column hero grid in `templates/content/workshops_list.html`.
- Production renders three `workshop-card-preview-fallback` nodes and zero `workshop-card-preview-image` nodes.
- `templates/_partials/mermaid_script.html` injects Mermaid layout CSS at the end of `<body>`. The designer measured a `0.064-0.129` layout shift on `/workshops/full-stack-vibe-coding/tutorial/overview`: content first moves down when `white-space: pre` arrives, then up when Mermaid replaces the source with an SVG.

Reference screenshots from the designer audit:

- `/workshops`, desktop: https://d31nukezbn4e3o.cloudfront.net/2026/07/13/c7de4d1fd1a349ab83900a24bf20bfa4-e2c6a2139952a6dc.png
- `/workshops`, Pixel 7: https://d31nukezbn4e3o.cloudfront.net/2026/07/13/ff2f7e702de4428685cb730d51164f44-c7e64eda7ba2f60e.png
- `/workshops/full-stack-vibe-coding`, desktop: https://d31nukezbn4e3o.cloudfront.net/2026/07/13/559272e3b0e44dda8f2566451d639d4b-7608db5340dfc59d.png
- `/workshops/full-stack-vibe-coding`, Pixel 7: https://d31nukezbn4e3o.cloudfront.net/2026/07/13/f675243499d84c1999d0fea51c4cccc8-b27d324dc5d924cd.png
- Tutorial page, desktop: https://d31nukezbn4e3o.cloudfront.net/2026/07/13/8eb65f0f069843698909a1a382c29880-af57f010d186c70a.png
- Tutorial page, Pixel 7: https://d31nukezbn4e3o.cloudfront.net/2026/07/13/64e65cff9750483a81a6dc8b5a4ff3a5-3d006b2c909dc830.png

### Workshop landing hierarchy (`GET /workshops`)

- Keep `/workshops` as the public landing-plus-preview route and `/workshops/catalog` as the filterable all-workshops catalog. Do not change URL names, redirects, authentication, publication filtering, or query parameters.
- In `templates/content/workshops_list.html`, replace the arbitrary-fraction two-column hero with one single-column landing header. The order is: `Workshops` eyebrow, one `h1`, one lead paragraph, and the existing CTA row.
- Keep the `h1` text `Hands-on AI workshops`, but use the documented page-heading scale `text-3xl font-semibold tracking-tight sm:text-4xl`; remove `lg:text-5xl`.
- Keep the first lead paragraph, beginning `Practical AI engineering sessions for builders...`, as the hero's only explanatory paragraph. Remove the second taxonomy paragraph beginning `Event pages announce live sessions...` from this hero; the product taxonomy remains documented and available through the rest of the site, but repeating it here makes the entry point too dense.
- Preserve the existing CTA labels and destinations: `Browse all workshops` goes to `/workshops/catalog`; `View membership options` goes to `/pricing`.
- Keep all three existing value points and their copy (`Guided build flow`, `Replay and writeups`, `Project outcomes`), but place them in a separate full-width row below the introduction/CTA block. Use the existing compact cards with `mt-10 grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-3`; do not retain any desktop `lg:grid-cols-1` side-stack override.
- Preserve the existing catalog preview below the hero, footer, newsletter surface, page title, meta description, and Mermaid script include.

### Workshop cards without a permanent placeholder (`GET /workshops` and `GET /workshops/catalog`)

- Preserve `Workshop.card_image_url` and the closed #1172 selection policy: explicit `cover_image_url` wins, then operator-selected `custom_banner_url`; generated `auto_banner_url` remains excluded from public card previews and remains available for OG/Twitter/Studio sharing.
- In `templates/content/_workshops_catalog.html`, render `content/_content_preview.html` only when `workshop.card_image_url` is non-empty. Remove the workshop call site's `preview_decorative_fallback=True` behavior.
- A workshop with no explicit cover/custom image must have no `aspect-video` media slot, no graduation-cap placeholder slab, no broken image, and no empty reserved media space. Its card begins with the existing text/body signals and remains a compact text-first card.
- A legacy or operator-managed workshop with a non-empty explicit `card_image_url` may still render its real image through the existing shared preview partial. Do not revive or introduce a workshop cover program, generate new images, or use `auto_banner_url` on cards.
- Preserve the card's existing type/access/skill badges, title, primary instructor, semantic date, description excerpt, tools, deliverables, tags, overflow count, focus behavior, full-card link, and route to `/workshops/<slug>`.
- Apply the same card policy to the unfiltered landing preview and every catalog filter result. Preserve access, skill, tool, and topic filters, active-filter summaries, clear-filter paths, pagination/limits, and member empty states.
- Keep `/workshops/<slug>` free of a duplicate cover/banner block above the title.

### Stable Mermaid layout on workshop detail and tutorial pages

- Move these three existing rules from the end-of-body `templates/_partials/mermaid_script.html` style block into the global `<style>` in the document `<head>` in `templates/base.html`, adjacent to the existing `.prose` image/table rules:
  - `div.mermaid { max-width: 100%; overflow-x: auto; }`
  - `div.mermaid > svg { max-width: none; height: auto; display: block; margin: 0 auto; }`
  - `div.mermaid:not([data-processed]) { white-space: pre; }`
- Remove only the duplicated `<style>` block from `_partials/mermaid_script.html`. Keep the lazy Mermaid module URL, deferred module script, self-guard, and conditional template includes unchanged.
- The unprocessed Mermaid source must receive its final pre-render layout rules before first body paint, so content below it does not move down later when an end-of-body style arrives. A single residual size change when the client-rendered SVG replaces source text is acceptable; the reported down-then-up double jump is not.
- Preserve local horizontal scrolling for wide diagrams, natural SVG width, readable mobile diagrams, and no page-level horizontal overflow. #1230 owns missing prose-container guards and broad wide-content containment; do not duplicate that issue here.
- Do not pursue font-swap shifts, server-side Mermaid rendering, fixed-height diagram frames, or intrinsic `width`/`height` attributes for synced prose images in this issue.

### API decision, data model, and integrations

- No model field, migration, content-sync change, production-data edit, Studio workflow, background job, integration setting, or authenticated production API endpoint is required.
- This is a public presentation and load-stability fix. It creates no operator action or operator-managed data workflow that would benefit from API coverage.
- Preserve existing workshop API/non-API boundaries and existing OG/Twitter banner precedence.

### Dependencies and overlap boundaries

- No open issue is a prerequisite. Closed #1165 established the landing page and closed #1172 established the card-specific image policy; this issue corrects the resulting layout and coverless fallback treatment.
- #1252 was closed as a duplicate and shipped no code.
- #1244 exclusively owns workshop topic/tool/outcome taxonomy and Browse by Topic redesign. Do not change filter classification or chip inventory here.
- #1230 owns wide prose containment and mobile panning. Preserve its changes if it lands first; this issue owns Mermaid style timing only.
- #1238 owns the design-system documentation rewrite. It must reconcile its Card Media Slots table with this approved workshop behavior; #1237 does not edit `_docs/design-system.md`.
- #1231 owns project-card media treatment. Do not generalize the workshop no-fallback decision to projects, courses, or other content types.
- Out of scope: workshop titles, metadata taxonomy, access rules, card badge redesign, new landing sections/subtopic groupings, content-repo cover creation, global button migration, event/workshop taxonomy, and server-side diagram rendering.

### Verification and screenshot expectations

- Update focused Django/template coverage in `content/tests/test_workshops_public.py` for the landing hierarchy and both coverless and explicit-image card paths. Reverse closed #1172 assertions that currently require a workshop fallback.
- Extend `content/tests/test_mermaid.py` or an equally focused template test to prove the three layout rules are emitted in the document head and are no longer emitted by the late partial, while lazy loading remains conditional.
- Update `playwright_tests/test_workshops.py` to cover the user journeys below. For load stability, delay the Mermaid module in a deterministic fixture and record the position of content immediately below the diagram from `DOMContentLoaded` until the module is released. The content must not move down due to late CSS; after release, Mermaid must still render and remain locally scrollable.
- Tester screenshot evidence is mandatory for `/workshops` and one diagram-bearing `/workshops/<slug>/tutorial/<page_slug>` at desktop `1280px` and mobile `393px`, in light and dark themes (8 screenshots total). The workshop fixtures must include at least two adjacent coverless cards. Read every screenshot and verify the intended page rendered, the hero has one clear column, coverless cards have no media slab or awkward reserved gap, card content remains aligned, diagrams are readable without body overflow, and there is no 404, stack trace, broken image, clipped CTA, or broken layout. Attach or link the screenshot set in one tester comment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Return HTTP 200 from anonymous `GET /workshops` and `GET /workshops/catalog` with all existing URL, publication, access, filter, and navigation behavior unchanged.
- [ ] Render `/workshops` with one single-column introduction ordered as eyebrow, `Hands-on AI workshops` page-scale `h1`, one lead paragraph, and the existing CTA row; omit the second `Event pages announce live sessions...` paragraph.
- [ ] Render the three existing value-point cards as a full-width row below the introduction, using one column on mobile and three columns from `sm` upward rather than a desktop side stack.
- [ ] Keep `Browse all workshops` linked to `/workshops/catalog` and `View membership options` linked to `/pricing`, with their existing keyboard-focus and 44px-target behavior.
- [ ] Render no preview node, `aspect-video` band, decorative fallback, broken image, or reserved media height for a workshop whose `card_image_url` is empty on both `/workshops` and `/workshops/catalog`.
- [ ] Continue rendering a real shared preview image for a workshop with an explicit `cover_image_url` or operator `custom_banner_url`, while never using `auto_banner_url` as a card image.
- [ ] Preserve all existing workshop-card text, badges, metadata, tools, deliverables, tags, full-card focus/link behavior, filtered results, and fresh/filter empty states after removing the coverless media band.
- [ ] Keep `/workshops/<slug>` free of a duplicate cover/banner preview and preserve existing workshop access, recording, tutorial, materials, and CTA behavior.
- [ ] Emit the three Mermaid layout rules from the document head before body content and remove the late inline style block from `_partials/mermaid_script.html` without duplicating the rules.
- [ ] Prevent content below a deterministic above-the-fold Mermaid fixture from moving down between `DOMContentLoaded` and delayed Mermaid module execution; allow only the residual source-to-SVG size change after rendering begins.
- [ ] Preserve lazy Mermaid rendering, processed SVG output, natural-width local horizontal scrolling, and no page-level horizontal overflow on workshop landing/detail/tutorial surfaces and other existing Mermaid-enabled content pages.
- [ ] Introduce no model field, migration, sync/data change, Studio action, IntegrationSetting, background job, or authenticated production API endpoint.
- [ ] Add focused Django/template regressions for hero hierarchy, coverless no-preview behavior, explicit-image precedence, filtered catalog parity, detail no-preview behavior, early Mermaid CSS, and conditional lazy-script behavior.
- [ ] Add or update `core` Playwright coverage for the user journeys below and make the relevant focused Django tests plus `make test-playwright-core` pass.
- [ ] Capture, read, and link the required 8 desktop/mobile light/dark screenshots; all show the expected hierarchy and compact coverless cards with no broken layout, image, diagram, CTA, horizontal body overflow, 404, or stack trace.

## Playwright Test Scenarios

### Scenario: Visitor understands workshops before choosing a next step
Given: An anonymous visitor wants to understand what a workshop offers before browsing
When: They open `/workshops`
Then: They read one concise introduction headed `Hands-on AI workshops`
Then: The three workshop value points follow below the introduction rather than competing in a side column
When: They activate `Browse all workshops`
Then: They arrive at `/workshops/catalog` and can use the existing catalog filters

### Scenario: Visitor compares workshop value with membership
Given: An anonymous visitor is on `/workshops` after reading the concise introduction and value points
When: They activate `View membership options`
Then: They arrive at `/pricing` and can compare the existing membership tiers

### Scenario: Visitor scans coverless workshops without a placeholder wall
Given: The landing preview and catalog contain at least two published workshops with no `cover_image_url` or `custom_banner_url`, including workshops that have `auto_banner_url`
When: An anonymous visitor scans `/workshops` and `/workshops/catalog`
Then: Each coverless card begins with its type/access signals and text content
Then: No card reserves a media slab or shows a graduation-cap fallback, broken image, or generated banner

### Scenario: Visitor opens a coverless workshop from its compact card
Given: An anonymous visitor sees a coverless workshop card on `/workshops/catalog`
When: They activate the card
Then: They arrive at `/workshops/<slug>`
Then: The existing title, access context, description, tutorial/recording/material actions, and membership path remain available
Then: No duplicate cover or fallback appears above the workshop title

### Scenario: Visitor still recognizes an explicitly illustrated legacy workshop
Given: A published workshop has an explicit `cover_image_url` or operator-selected `custom_banner_url`, and also has an `auto_banner_url`
When: An anonymous visitor sees its card in the catalog and opens it
Then: The card uses the explicit real image rather than the generated banner
Then: The detail page continues to use the existing text-first header without a duplicate preview

### Scenario: Visitor filters compact workshop cards without changing their media policy
Given: `/workshops/catalog` contains coverless Free and paid workshops across multiple existing filter values
When: A visitor selects an access, skill, tool, or topic filter and later clears it
Then: The matching cards and active-filter summary update through the existing URL/query behavior
Then: Coverless filtered cards remain text-first with no placeholder media band
Then: Clearing returns to the existing unfiltered catalog journey

### Scenario: Visitor gets a useful empty catalog after narrowing too far
Given: An anonymous visitor chooses an existing workshop filter combination with no matches
When: The filtered catalog responds
Then: The canonical filter-empty state explains that nothing matched and offers the existing route back to all workshops
Then: No empty media placeholders or broken card grid appear

### Scenario: Workshop learner reads a Mermaid tutorial without the down-then-up jump
Given: An eligible visitor opens an above-the-fold Mermaid tutorial while the Mermaid module response is deliberately delayed
When: The document body first renders
Then: The unprocessed diagram already uses its preformatted, locally scrollable layout
Then: Content immediately below the diagram does not move down because of a late style injection
When: The module is released
Then: The diagram renders to SVG and the rest of the tutorial journey remains usable

### Scenario: Workshop learner pans a wide rendered diagram without moving the page
Given: An eligible visitor opens a workshop detail or tutorial page with a diagram wider than the reading column
When: They pan the rendered diagram at desktop and mobile widths
Then: The diagram stays at a readable natural width inside its local horizontal scroll area
Then: The document itself does not gain horizontal scrolling
Then: Existing reader navigation, completion, and Questions & Answers actions remain available

title: AI Briefing Request - 2026-07-13 16:00 UTC+8
content:
@codex Please create today's PulseMind software-engineer AI radar as a pull request.

Date: 2026-07-13

Goal:
Create a high-signal Chinese curated digest for software engineers. It should collect, organize, and publish AI-related news, technical blogs, tools, papers, and engineering practice that software engineers would actually want to open, read, try, or track.

Focus areas:
- AI application development: RAG, agents, tool use, MCP, memory, evals, observability, orchestration, prompt engineering, AI product architecture
- Large models and model platforms: model releases, APIs, SDKs, inference cost, latency, deployment, routing, fine-tuning, multimodal capabilities
- Coding agents and developer tools: IDE agents, code generation, code review, test generation, debugging, documentation, CI/CD, browser/web agents
- Frontend and backend development: React, Next.js, Vue, Svelte, Node.js, Python, Go, Java, Rust, databases, APIs, cloud, DevOps, and architecture when the item helps engineers build software better
- Open-source projects, technical blogs, benchmarks, engineering case studies, implementation notes, and postmortems
- Security and governance engineers need to understand: prompt injection, jailbreaks, data leakage, supply chain risk, permission boundaries, auditability
- Research only when it includes a method, benchmark, limitation, or result that application engineers can learn from

Audience:
Chinese software engineers, engineering managers, technical founders, and AI application builders. They care about practical technical signal: what changed, what is worth reading, what is worth trying, what risk to watch, and what engineering idea can be reused. They do not want general AI business news, consumer product commentary, funding summaries, or broad industry trend essays unless there is a direct engineering implication.

Task:
Create exactly one Markdown article under `content/articles/`, named:
`2026-07-13-<short-slug>.md`

Only edit `content/articles/**/*.md`.

Language:
Use Simplified Chinese.

Length:
1200-1800 Chinese characters.

Article type:
This is a software-engineer AI radar / curated reading digest, not a single-theme essay, broad opinion article, company news roundup, funding digest, or press release rewrite.

Source selection:
- Candidate sources are roughly pre-ranked by software-engineering relevance first and recency second. Treat the order as a hint, not as proof of quality.
- Select 4 to 7 items from the candidate sources.
- Select fewer items if only a few are genuinely useful to software engineers.
- Do not force all selected items into one theme. It is acceptable and preferred to publish a curated list across AI application development, large models, coding agents, frontend, and backend engineering.
- The final result must feel like a hand-curated engineering reading list, not a synthetic industry analysis essay.
- Do not include a source only because the company is famous.
- Prefer items that satisfy at least one of the following:
  - a tool, API, framework, SDK, benchmark, library, repo, tutorial, or architecture worth trying
  - a technical blog or case study with implementation detail, tradeoff, metric, failure mode, or reproducible lesson
  - a concrete workflow change for frontend/backend development, coding, testing, review, debugging, documentation, CI/CD, or operations
  - a production engineering lesson about reliability, cost, latency, evals, observability, safety, data, deployment, or model routing
  - a security or governance risk that changes how engineers should design AI applications or agent systems
  - a model, paper, or benchmark that changes how engineers should evaluate, deploy, or integrate LLMs
- Deprioritize or skip:
  - consumer AI product reviews without engineering detail
  - funding, IPO, or valuation news without technical substance
  - company strategy stories without developer impact
  - sensational controversy without an engineering lesson
  - vague "AI changes everything" commentary
  - one-sentence social posts unless they point to a concrete tool, repo, metric, production constraint, or developer workflow

Required article structure:
1. Curated items:
   - Start directly with the first curated item after the frontmatter.
   - Do not write an opening paragraph, editor's note, column note, format explanation, or transition paragraph.
   - Use 4 to 7 short sections.
   - Each section covers exactly one selected item.
   - Start each section title with one label from:
     - `AI 应用`
     - `大模型`
     - `Coding Agent`
     - `前端/后端`
     - `工具/开源`
     - `安全/治理`
   - Each section must answer:
     - What is the item? Include a Markdown link.
     - What is the useful technical detail?
     - Why should software engineers care?
     - What should readers read, try, monitor, or avoid next?
2. No closing summary:
   - Do not add a closing paragraph.
   - End after the final curated item and its engineering takeaway.

Source grounding:
- Use only the candidate sources provided below.
- Each selected item must include a Markdown link to the source in the body.
- Do not invent facts not present in the provided title, snippet, or accessible source page.
- If the source page is unavailable or unclear, do not use that item.
- Prefer concrete facts over interpretation.
- When discussing research, focus on the problem, method, result, limitation, and possible practical impact.
- If a source lacks enough technical detail, say less about it or skip it.

Style:
- Clear, concise, editorial.
- Write like a senior software engineer curating useful links for other engineers, not like a marketing writer or industry analyst.
- Do not include meta commentary about the article format, editorial intent, issue window, source selection, or what the article is not.
- Do not use phrases such as:
  - 这期雷达
  - 本期雷达
  - 本文覆盖
  - 下面不是
  - 这不是
  - 可读、可试、可跟进
  - 工程清单
  - 本文/本篇/这篇文章
- Use engineering vocabulary only when it clarifies the point. Avoid jargon-padding.
- Avoid hype, slogans, and vague abstractions.
- Avoid these phrases unless backed by concrete facts:
  - 赋能
  - 生态闭环
  - 底层逻辑
  - 范式转移
  - 从工具到基础设施
  - 更可用、更可管、更可扩
  - 重塑行业
  - 引领未来
- Avoid listing company names without explaining the concrete value.
- Every item should contain at least one specific fact, tool, repo, framework, product, metric, scenario, engineering practice, or research result.
- Every item should end with a concrete takeaway for engineers.

Frontmatter:
Use this shape:

```yaml
---
title: "中文标题"
slug: "url-safe-slug"
summary: "100 字以内摘要"
category: "ai"
tags:
  - AI

source: "primary-source-url"
```

Title requirements:
- The title should describe the briefing's actual content.
- Avoid vague titles like "AI 行业正在发生变化".
- Prefer concrete titles, for example:
  - "软件工程师 AI 雷达：Coding Agent、MCP 与前后端开发"

Source guide:
- Hacker News: 优先选全球工程师、创业者正在讨论的 AI 应用、大模型、coding-agent、开源项目、前后端开发工具和技术争议；跳过只有情绪或八卦价值的讨论。
- Hacker News LLM Search: 补充 HN 最新提交中的 LLM、AI 应用、coding-agent、开发者工具和工程实践讨论，优先选指向 GitHub、技术博客、论文或可试用工具的条目。
- The Verge AI: 只在产品、安全、平台政策或行业争议对 AI 应用开发、模型集成、数据使用、权限边界、用户体验设计有工程启发时采用；跳过纯消费产品评论。
- TechCrunch AI: 只在创业产品、平台、API、SDK、基础设施、定价、部署方式或商业化路径对开发者有参考价值时采用；跳过纯融资新闻和硬件体验文。
- QbitAI: 优先选国内外模型、Agent、框架、论文、工程实践、开发者工具、前后端 AI 应用案例的技术细节；跳过只有公司动态或热闹标题的内容。
- arXiv cs.AI/cs.CL: 重点抓可复用的方法、评测、限制和潜在工程影响；只选会影响 AI 应用、coding-agent、RAG、推理、模型部署或开发工具的论文。
- BestBlogs.dev: 优先选工程师、研究员和创业者的高质量 AI 技术博客，尤其是带实现细节、架构取舍、踩坑经验、评测方法、前后端工程实践或可复现实验的长文；跳过缺少技术细节的社交短帖。
